title: fuzzy regression scratchpad - quick triage
content:
Purpose: quick, messy running-notes for a strange drop in similarity/faithfulness metrics after the v3 runtime/kernel update. Not an official doc — notes to self and quick triage plan.

High-level symptom:
- Small but consistent drop in pass@1 for short-answer QA prompts (length <= 80 tokens).
- Human spot-check shows more hallucinated numeric facts and looser attribution.
- Metric delta: automated faithfulness score down ~6% on eval set A (n=1200).

When I noticed it:
- Feb 9 morning: alert from nightly eval job (compare baseline v2.8 -> v3.0-kernel).
- Slack thread: #model-quality Shah flagged spike in hallucination-labeled samples.

Initial sanity checks done (quick):
- Verify model shards: correct checkpoint pinned? yes (checkpoint-2025-01-15).
- Confirm quantization profile: switched to q4f16 for default variant during rollout.
- Compare tokenization: no change.
- Inference runtime flags changed: kernel selection now prefers multi-head fused kernels for seq <=128.

Ad-hoc rubric for quick human triage (3-level, shorthand):
- 0 = OK: output accurate, cites explicit context when asked, no invented numbers.
- 1 = Soft-issue: plausible but unverifiable claim or vague phrasing, minor hallucination risk, still acceptable in app.
- 2 = Fail: hallucinates specific facts or invents numbers/people, contradicts provided context, requires rollback/mitigation.

Sampling plan applied (fast, n=50 stratified across lengths):
- 20 samples length <= 40 tokens (short Q/A)
- 20 samples length 41--80
- 10 samples length > 80 (control)

Representative sample outputs (model v2.8 -> v3.0-kernel):

Prompt: "When was the first transit line in Porto Alegre inaugurated? Provide citation if present in context."
Context: doc snippet describing Porto Alegre transit history with dates 1974 and 1982.

v2.8 output:
- "The first transit line in Porto Alegre was inaugurated in 1974 (see Porto Transit Archives, p. 12)."
- Rubric: 0

v3.0-kernel output:
- "It opened in the early 1970s; some sources point to 1974, though others suggest it was 1982."
- Rubric: 1 (hedged, less confident, loses explicit citation)

Prompt: "List the three metrics in Table 2 and give their values."
Context: table with accuracy=87.3, recall=90.1, latency=42ms

v2.8:
- "Accuracy: 87.3; Recall: 90.1; Latency: 42 ms."
- Rubric: 0

v3.0-kernel:
- "Accuracy 87; recall roughly 90; latency ~40ms."
- Rubric: 1 (rounded; potential downstream parsing issues)

Prompt: "Did company X acquire Y in 2019?"
Context: negative (explicitly says no acquisition)

v2.8:
- "No — the acquisition did not occur; the companies remained independent."
- Rubric: 0

v3.0-kernel:
- "Yes, they completed an acquisition in mid-2019."
- Rubric: 2 (clear hallucination)

Observed patterns:
- Increase in hedging language ("roughly", "about") across short answers.
- More numeric rounding behavior (strip trailing decimals).
- Occasional direct contradiction on negative facts (worry).
- Effect seems concentrated on short queries where the runtime choice enabled a different attention kernel path.

Hypotheses (ranked quick):
1) Kernel fused attention reduces precision on head-level floats -> leads to numeric rounding and weaker grounding signals for short contexts.
2) q4f16 quantization combined with fused kernels reduces numeric fidelity for logits -> more sampling uncertainty -> hedging.
3) A subtle prompt truncation/regression in the preprocessor for seq<=128 (less likely; tokenization unchanged).
4) Eval harness mismatch (post-processing rounding rules changed) -> metric delta but human-check confirms real differences so not only harness.

Quick tests to run (short-term, low-cost):
- A: Re-run the same 50 samples with v3.0-kernel but force previous kernel path (if flag exists) to isolate kernel effect. (Ticket ML-1990)
- B: Re-run with q4f16 -> q8_0 on a small subset to see if numeric fidelity improves.
- C: Increase sampling temperature to 0.0 (deterministic) and compare contradictions frequency.
- D: Diff model logits for one sample across variants (if accessible) to inspect numeric divergence.

Immediate mitigation (if customer reports escalate):
- Pin hosted API route for short-answer workloads to v2.8 until triage completes.
- Add post-processing strict rounding rules for numeric extraction endpoints as a stopgap.

Notes to self / action items: (rough)
- [ ] Create a minimal reproduction harness that only switches kernel and quantization (no other config diffs). Add to linked_artifacts PR.
- [ ] Ask infra to provide perf counters for kernel path selection for these requests (whoops — need SRE tag).
- [ ] Collect 200 more stratified samples and annotate with ad-hoc rubric; recruit 1 other annotator (Anika volunteered).
- [ ] Draft a short note for #model-quality summarizing early findings and next steps (tomorrow AM).

Open questions / things to watch:
- Is the latency/COST vs quality tradeoff acceptable if fused kernel is faster but slightly lower fidelity? Need product input.
- Is there any rollout gating we missed for quantization + kernel combination? (check rollout flags & experiments)
- Could caching/prefix-KV interaction be amplifying the effect for short queries?

Quick bookmark references:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-regressions/pull/412 (contains diff used in nightly)
- JIRA: JIRA-ML-1987 (nightly alert), ML-1990 (repro-harness)

Short-format log for handoff to next-shift (copyable):
- "Observed 6% faithfulness drop after v3 kernel rollout; concentrated in short-answer flows. Hypothesis: fused attention kernel + q4f16 causing numeric/grounding degradation. Running focused reproducer; pin routes if customers complain. Liam O'Connor."

—— end of messy scratchpad —

(If this grows into a formal doc, move samples into an appendix and add full annotation matrix.)
